paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves over a series of iterations for six different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four variations of SepLLM. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with numeric tick labels spaced at regular intervals of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and employs a linear scale with a value range from 2.4 to 3.4, featuring numeric tick labels at intervals of 0.1. All six configurations are represented by solid lines without markers, each surrounded by a lighter shaded region of corresponding color. All lines exhibit a similar overall trend: beginning off the top of the chart above a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0, they undergo a rapid, steep decline within the first 20,000 iterations before transitioning into a steady, gradual decrease toward the end of the plotted range. By the final iteration of 140,000, the lines separate into distinct final values. The light purple line representing the "Vanilla" model reaches the lowest final loss value of approximately 2.47. Resting slightly above it is the red line for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" which ends near 2.49, closely followed by the dark blue line for "SepLLM (n=128)" concluding roughly at 2.50. The green line corresponding to "SepLLM (n=64, H)" arrives at a loss of about 2.51, while the orange line for "SepLLM (n=64)" ends slightly higher at approximately 2.53. Finally, the light blue line representing "StrmLLM (n=64)" maintains the highest loss curve upon stabilization, ending at approximately 2.61 at 140,000 iterations.
